title: Historic buildings and structures
amount_raw: Generally, £1,000 to £30,000 (average approx. £15,000). Sometimes larger sums are considered.
eligibility_summary: UK registered charities, organisations with exempt charitable status, recognised public bodies, Community Benefit Societies or CICs limited by guarantee. Project must be UK based, focus on a listed building/structure, and not be complete (no retrospective grants). Individuals may not apply.
summary: Two-stage rolling grants for the preservation and repair of listed historic buildings, structures and architectural features, with special consideration for sustainable re-use of at-risk buildings of outstanding importance. Stage one rolling; grants of £5,000 or less considered on a rolling basis; Stage two applications over £5,000 decided at quarterly Trustee meetings (Mar, Jun, Sep, Nov).
notes: Own scheme page. Status open: applications accepted at any time (Stage 1 rolling; small grants <=GBP5,000 rolling). Deadlines are the 2026 Stage-two cut-offs for grants over GBP5,000: 9 Jan, 10 Apr, 31 Jul, 2 Oct (9 Jan/10 Apr/31 Jul are past on the 2026-08-21 snapshot; 2 Oct remains open). Recorded all four as the published round deadlines per staged/multi-deadline handling. restricted: institutional applicants only (charities/public bodies/CBS/CIC), no individuals. Also listed on grants-at-a-glance and preservation-and-conservation-grants hub. FLAG FOR REVIEW: many Pilgrim grantees are museums/charities/local trusts rather than individual researchers; scheme is open to some UK-based researchers only via their host institution.

title: Places of worship
eligibility_summary: UK registered charities, exempt charitable status organisations and recognised public bodies. Anglican churches must apply via the ChurchCare conservation grants scheme (part-funded by Pilgrim Trust); all other denominations, faiths and cathedrals apply directly. No longer funds repair of places of worship open for regular worship except conservation of historic interiors and historic objects. Individuals may not apply.
summary: Grants for the conservation of historic interiors and historic objects (bells, manuscripts, clocks, plasterwork, metalwork, monuments, organs, paintings, stained glass, textiles, timberwork, wall paintings, churchyard structures) in places of worship open for regular worship, plus commissioning of conservation reports. Two-stage; Stage one rolling, Stage two over GBP5,000 decided quarterly.
notes: Own scheme page. Status open on same rolling/quarterly mechanism as Historic buildings (2026 cut-offs 9 Jan, 10 Apr, 31 Jul, 2 Oct). Page gives no explicit grant-size range (amounts uncertain; the GBP1,000-GBP30,000 P&C band on sibling pages may apply but is not stated here). ambiguous_eligibility: Anglican church interiors must route to the external ChurchCare scheme, only other denominations/cathedrals apply direct to Pilgrim. restricted: institutional applicants only. Buildings/repair applications now redirected to Historic buildings and structures.

title: Grants for collections and objects
eligibility_summary: UK registered charities, exempt charitable status organisations, recognised public bodies, Community Benefit Societies or CICs limited by guarantee; must NOT be eligible for the AIM or NMCT partner grant schemes. Project must be UK based and not complete. Individuals may not apply.
summary: Two-stage rolling grants for the conservation of culturally and historically significant collections and objects (works of art, books, ephemera, artefacts, archives). Conservation must be by an accredited conservator, informed by a conservation report, and enable greater public access. Stage one rolling; grants of GBP5,000 or less rolling; Stage two over GBP5,000 decided quarterly (Mar, Jun, Sep, Nov). Museums/manuscripts routed to AIM/NMCT partners first.
notes: Own scheme page (mirror title 'Grants for collections and objects'; H1 'Conservation of cultural heritage'; title recorded verbatim from the page H1 area / nav). Status open on rolling+quarterly mechanism (2026 cut-offs 9 Jan, 10 Apr, 31 Jul, 2 Oct). restricted: institutional applicants only, and applicants eligible for AIM/NMCT partner schemes must apply there instead. FLAG FOR REVIEW: title choice - nav label vs page heading vs mirror <title> 'Grants for collections and objects'; used the page's own heading area label.

title: Archives Revealed
eligibility_summary: UK registered charities, exempt charitable status organisations and recognised public bodies; work must be UK based and not complete. Applications made via The National Archives, not directly to Pilgrim Trust. Individuals may not apply.
summary: Partnership funding programme (The National Archives, National Lottery Heritage Fund, Pilgrim Trust, Wolfson Foundation) - the only UK grant programme dedicated to cataloguing and unlocking archival collections. Includes Scoping Grants (funding an independent consultant to produce an expert collections/scoping report) and cataloguing grants.
notes: Own scheme page. Applications handled entirely on The National Archives website (external to this mirror) - the Pilgrim page carries no deadlines, amounts or round dates, so status/deadlines/amounts are uncertain and defaulted to rolling (page presents it as an ongoing programme with no closed/expired language). restricted: institutional applicants only. js_portal/pdf_only: scheme detail (rounds, amounts, forms) lives on the external National Archives portal and in the linked 2019 brochure PDF, not captured as scheme pages here. FLAG FOR REVIEW: cannot confirm current open round or amounts from the mirror; news page 'Archives Revealed awards eight new scoping grants' (Jan 2026) is a grantee-announcement distractor, not a separate row.

title: Research, advocacy and development fund
eligibility_summary: Projects, ideas and organisations doing research, advocacy or sector-development work in young women's mental health or preservation and conservation of historic buildings and collections. Normally by invitation: the Trust builds partnerships and then invites applications; prospective applicants email the Director to discuss a proposal. Not an open call.
summary: A small strategic fund for research, advocacy and development work that could bring systemic change, drive policy and practice, or strengthen the sector, in the Trust's areas of interest (young women's mental health; preservation and conservation of historic buildings and collections; increasing access to the countryside). Conversational/relationship-based rather than an open application round.
notes: Own scheme page. Included as in_scope=yes because it invites conversations/proposals with no closing date (treated as rolling), and is available to UK-based researchers/organisations doing research and advocacy work. HEAVILY restricted/ambiguous: the Trust 'normally build[s] partnerships and then invite[s] applications' (invitation-based, small pot) and states it is 'unlikely to support further research and advocacy work in the young women's mental health field' as proposals are already under development. FLAG FOR REVIEW: borderline - this is more an expression-of-interest/invitation route than an open call; a stricter reading (no open application process) would set in_scope=no. No amounts or deadlines given.

title: Young Women in Mind 2026-2028
amount_raw: Grant size: £200,000 to £500,000 spread over three years.
eligibility_summary: UK registered charities (for at least three years) already delivering therapeutic mental health services: either a mental health charity with a clear youth and mental health mission and annual income GBP750,000+, OR a specialist charity led by and for women and girls with a mental health mission, experience delivering services to under-18s and annual income GBP350,000+. Must operate in Northern Ireland, Scotland, or the England regions North East, North West, Yorkshire and Humber, or the Midlands (UK-wide/England-wide orgs may apply for work across their remit).
summary: Collaborative funding programme (Pilgrim Trust, Prudence Trust, Julia Rausing Trust) investing GBP5m over 2026-2028 to strengthen and scale gender-specific therapeutic mental health services for girls and young women aged 14-25.
exclusion_reason: Page states 'This grant programme has now closed for this year and we are no longer accepting applications' as of the 2026-08-21 snapshot - not accepting new applications and no future open date stated. The 24 Aug 2026 stage-two deadline applies only to already-invited stage-one applicants, not new applicants.
notes: Distractor. Programme opened 11 May 2026; stage one deadline 22 Jun 2026 (past), stage two deadline 24 Aug 2026 (for those who passed stage one only). Explicitly closed to new applicants on the snapshot date. FAQ says geographical reach may expand in future years but gives no next open date, so excluded rather than forthcoming. Amounts/eligibility captured for the record. FLAG FOR REVIEW: stage-two deadline 24 Aug 2026 is 3 days after the snapshot but is not a new-applicant entry point.

title: Strategic partners
eligibility_summary: Not directly applicable - partners (Church Building Council/ChurchCare, National Manuscripts Conservation Trust, Architectural Heritage Fund, Association of Independent Museums, Theatres Trust) run their own grant programmes and distribute Pilgrim Trust funds; eligible projects apply to the partner, not to Pilgrim directly.
summary: Informational page describing the Trust's heritage strategic partners, who distribute Pilgrim Trust funds (around GBP500,000 last year) through their own grant programmes and provide sector expertise.
exclusion_reason: Informational/routing page, not a distinct Pilgrim Trust call - the funding is delivered through separate partner-run schemes (ChurchCare, NMCT, AHF, AIM, Theatres Trust) to which applicants apply externally. No own application process, deadline or amount.
notes: Distractor. Lists five strategic partners who administer Pilgrim funds via their own programmes; 'if a project is eligible for grant support from one of our partners, it is not eligible to apply direct to us.' Not a scheme row. The partner schemes themselves live on external sites (not captured).
